A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDJE research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDJE retrieval results on Flickr30k and COCO, efficiency measurements, and token-count, training-objective, and distillation ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original storage-I/O measurements, semantic analyses, larger-candidate retrieval evaluations, and compression, quantization, negative-mining, and text-encoder experiments.

M1.justification: The core adapter, joint encoder, training objectives, and distillation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix H adds an evaluated deployment variant that quantizes cached tokens to FP8 or FP4 and dequantizes them before inference, without further fine-tuning. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: The training corpora and evaluated image-text retrieval tasks remain unchanged. Flickr Full and COCO Full expand candidate pools using existing dataset splits, constituting protocol changes rather than new dataset or task coverage. Appendix I proposes video extensions but reports no video evaluation.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets in Tables 1-2 are retained. v2 adds LightningDOT comparisons in Tables 8-9 and matched compression comparisons against striding, k-means++ clustering, and attention pruning in Table 10. Table 11 additionally compares BERT-Base with MiniLM, substantially expanding comparative evidence.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings are retained, while new experiments introduce full-dataset candidate pools, k=100, and Recall@5/10/20; controlled 64-token compression comparisons; alternative negative miners and text encoders; and BF16/FP8/FP4 storage conditions. Appendices C-D also introduce contiguous versus random-access SSD timing and caption-preprocessed token-alignment evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained token-count, pool-size, objective, and distillation ablations, v2 investigates token semantics and caption alignment, cross-model negative mining, alternative compression mechanisms, quantization robustness, and text-encoder capacity. The new I/O analysis also tests a deployment cost omitted from v1's compute-focused efficiency evaluation.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without comparable uncertainty reporting. Appendix C.1 newly reports I/O timing variability and explicitly identifies 10 runs for contiguous loading. Appendix D.2 reports alignment means with plus/minus spreads, a paired two-sided t-test, and effect size. These additions are limited to supplementary measurements; retrieval tables still lack repeated-training uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and the original ablation results in Tables 4-5 are unchanged. Substantial new results include Flickr Full text-to-image R@5 of 78.32 versus LightningDOT's 60.1 in Table 8, and 64-token Flickr text-to-image R@1 of 86.9 for EDJE versus 85.66 for clustering in Table 10. Further additions cover I/O, alignment, mining, quantization, and BERT. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements to retained v1 scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly defines the diagnostic image-caption alignment score as the average, over caption tokens, of maximum cosine similarity to visual tokens. The original adapter equations and training losses remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims: offline vision computation, learned token compression, efficient joint encoding, and competitive retrieval. The headline 50k pairs/second and 49 kB/image claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations linking compression to semantic redundancy removal and preserved alignment, negative-miner strength to retrieval quality, and limited BERT gains to adequate MiniLM capacity at the studied training scale. Appendix C qualifies deployment claims through storage-I/O costs and advises against networked storage. Appendix I develops previously unelaborated video-extension possibilities.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the forthcoming implementation/checkpoint promise with a stated public code link and adds offline indexing and online retrieval pseudocode. New documentation specifies SSD access layouts, token precision and quantization procedures, caption preprocessing, and compression-baseline construction. The original hyperparameter table is retained; these additions substantially improve documented implementation and deployment guidance.

R1.justification: Related work adds a focused discussion distinguishing EDJE from LightningDOT's cached region representations. References to LightningDOT, BERT, and two video-related works support the new comparisons and proposed extensions. The broader positioning among embedding models, joint encoders, and generative VLMs remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. v2 standardizes 're-ranking', updates publication and citation formatting, adds cross-references and Section 5.4, renames Appendix B, and organizes new appendices. The expansion does not constitute extensive rewriting of the original exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds semantic word-cloud displays, an alignment histogram, a quantization/storage plot, Tables 6-11, and two pseudocode algorithms. Figures 4-5 move from vertically stacked, text-wrapped placement to a side-by-side arrangement. Figure 6's example is repeated within Figure 7. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central efficiency and compression argument: v1 lacked matched alternative-compression baselines and measurements of token-fetch costs, both now addressed in Appendices G and C. Larger-candidate retrieval tests, failure-sensitive ablations, and practical implementation guidance further improve validation and usability. Localized editing problems remain: Figure 9's caption describes lower alignment despite higher reported compressed-token means, and Appendix J quotes R@10=97.98 where Table 11 shows 97.9. These weaken particular statements but do not outweigh the substantial gains in supporting evidence.
